scenes.narration: Your coding agent just rebuilt a login system. From scratch. Again.
And a content model. And search. On every single project.

scenes.callout: Code is cheap. Owning it isn't.
scenes.narration: Here's the thing nobody tells you. Generating code got cheap. Owning it didn't.
Every line your agent writes is a line someone has to secure, debug and maintain. Forever.
Meanwhile, open source has spent more than twenty years on exactly these problems. Millions of sites. Battle-tested. Already patched.
And agents? They're amazing at wiring proven pieces together. That's their superpower. Not rebuilding them.

scenes.callout: First ask: what can we reuse?
scenes.narration: So here's my rule. Before your agent writes a single line, ask what you can reuse. Users, permissions, content, search.
Then let it spend all that energy on the part that makes your app yours.

points: Code is cheap, owning it isn't
scenes.narration: Code is cheap, owning it isn't. Reuse what's proven. Build what's unique.
That's what we're exploring at Proven Lab. Now tell me: what does your agent keep rebuilding? Drop it in the comments.
